narara.summary: Walk on a living coral reef at low tide, inside India's first Marine National Park.
narara.overview:
Most people think you need a scuba licence to see coral. At Narara you need a pair of old shoes and the right tide.

Narara is part of the Marine National Park in the Gulf of Kutch. Twice a month the sea pulls back far enough to uncover the reef, and you walk out in knee-deep water with a guide. Look down and the floor is alive: corals, starfish, crabs, sea anemones and, if you are patient, an octopus changing colour to hide from you.

The brochure our founder wrote for this trip counted 37 kinds of hard and soft coral, about 30 kinds of crabs and more than 100 kinds of seaweed. You will not spot them all. You will spot more than you expect.

itinerary.body: Early start from Rajkot, breakfast on the way. Reach Narara and walk the reef at low tide with our guide. Lunch, then a second walk around the island while the tide is still out, following the tide rules. Coastal walk and bird watching. Head home in the evening.

faqs.question: Do I need to know swimming?
faqs.answer: No. You walk on the reef in knee-deep water at low tide. Our guide sets the route and the time to come back.

faqs.question: Is it safe to walk on coral?
faqs.answer: Only on the marked route and only with a guide. We walk slowly, step on rock and sand, and never pick up or break anything alive.

faqs.question: What should I wear on my feet?
faqs.answer: Closed shoes that can get wet. The reef is sharp in places, so slippers and bare feet are a no.

faqs.question: Can I book just for myself?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you are 18 or older you can join any open batch and travel with the group.

faqs.question: What if the tide or weather is wrong?
faqs.answer: We plan the date around the tide table. If the weather turns, our leaders change the plan for safety.

bet-dwarka-marine-camp.summary: Where CNA began: island days in the Gulf of Kutch, with mangroves, boat trips and sea life at low tide.
bet-dwarka-marine-camp.overview:
On day three, lunch is served on a boat that will not sit still. Plates slide, someone laughs, and then a fin breaks the water and everyone forgets the food.

Bet Dwarka is a small island in the Gulf of Kutch, a short crossing from Okha. The water around it is calm and clear, and it holds a rich treasure of marine life: corals, starfish, sea anemones, crabs and, on lucky days, dolphins and sea turtles. We walk the mangroves near camp, take the boat out to the smaller islands and learn how the tide and the moon decide what you get to see.

This is where our story starts. CNA's very first camp was a marine camp at Bet, in December 1997. We still run it from our partner campus on the island, with the same idea: let the sea teach.

The island also has deep roots in the Krishna story. Bet was his home, and Dwarka the seat of his kingdom, so the temples are part of the trip too.

itinerary.body: After breakfast we take the boat out to the nearby islands, such as Dunni, Churna, Dabdaba and Sindhi, to watch marine life. Lunch on the boat. We land only when the tide and weather are safe, and come back to camp by evening. Campfire and star gazing.

itinerary.body: After breakfast, on to Dwarka. A scuba diving introduction with trained experts and a talk on life under the sea, then darshan at the Jagat Mandir (Dwarkadhish temple). Evening train home.

faqs.question: Will we see dolphins?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. Dolphins and sea turtles visit these waters, but nobody can promise a sighting. Corals, starfish, crabs and sea birds you will see for sure.

faqs.question: Is this a pilgrimage trip?

faqs.question: Why only October to March?

sasan-gir.summary: Three days in lion country: a jeep safari, walks by the Hiran river and campfire nights in tents.
sasan-gir.overview:
Walk along the Hiran river in the late afternoon and look at the mud on the banks. Those big pug marks are not from a dog. This is the river where Gir's lions come to drink.

Gir is the only place in the world where the Asiatic lion still lives in the wild. The forest was protected in 1965 and covers about 1,412 sq km of dry teak and scrub. Lions are the headline, but the cast is bigger: around 38 kinds of mammals, about 300 kinds of birds, crocodiles in the rivers and leopards that most people never see.

We stay in tents near Talala, on the edge of the forest. Days are for a jeep safari, forest walks and a waterfall trail. Nights are for the campfire, and one of them for the dhamal dance of Gir's Siddi community.

itinerary.body: After breakfast, a jeep safari at Devalia to look for lions (permits subject to availability). Evening walk along the banks of the Hiran river. After dinner, folk raas at the campfire.

faqs.question: Why does this camp run only November to March?
faqs.answer: The Gir national park closes to visitors in the monsoon. From November the forest is open, dry and pleasant to walk in.

faqs.question: Is it safe to camp so close to the forest?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our tents are on a private site outside the forest, our leaders stay with the group all the time, and we follow forest department rules on every walk.

faqs.question: Who are the Siddi people?
faqs.answer: A community that has lived in and around Gir for centuries, with roots in East Africa. Their dhamal dance at the campfire is a highlight of the camp.

osam-hill.summary: A one-day hill walk two hours from Rajkot, with old temples, Bhim Kund and a Pandava legend at the top.
osam-hill.overview:
Local legend says the Pandavas hid on this hill during their exile, and that giant Bhim ate his meals off a stone plate that is still up there. Nobody can prove it. Everybody still goes to look.

Osam Hill rises above Patanvav village, near Upleta, about two hours from Rajkot. The walk up is easy and the hill packs a lot into one day: rock formations, the Mataji and Tapkeshwar temples, old forts, and Bhim Kund, a natural pool of water among the rocks.

Come in the monsoon and the whole hill turns green. Come in winter and the air is clear enough to see across the plains. It is our favourite first outing for school groups and families, and a good test for anyone who wants to try a longer trek later.

itinerary.title: Up and around Osam
itinerary.body: Early start from Rajkot, breakfast at the foot of the hill. Walk up Osam Hill and around the top: temples, rock formations, Bhim Kund and the view. Lunch, then a walk through Patanvav village and the places around it. Back in Rajkot by evening.

faqs.question: Is Osam Hill good for a first trek?
faqs.answer: Yes. The walk is short and easy, the trail is clear and you are back home the same night. Many people start here.

faqs.question: When is the best time to go?
faqs.answer: July to February. The hill is greenest just after the rains, and winter mornings are cool and clear. Summer afternoons get very hot.

faqs.question: Can small children come?
faqs.answer: Yes, with their family. The walk is easy, and our leaders set a pace that works for the slowest walker.

faqs.question: Is it safe in the monsoon?
faqs.answer: Yes, with care. Rocks get slippery, so wear shoes with grip. If heavy rain makes a section unsafe, our leaders change the route.

hingolgadh-nature-camp.summary: A hilltop palace, about 230 kinds of birds and a night under the stars, a short drive from Rajkot.
hingolgadh-nature-camp.overview:
Hingolgadh was once famous for breeding Kathiyawadi horses. The horses are mostly gone. The birds never left: about 230 kinds of them live in or pass through this small sanctuary.

The hill stands about 1,000 feet high in Jasdan taluka, a short drive from Rajkot, with a palace on top built by the Khachar rulers in the 17th century. Around it is dry forest, grassland, check dams and small rivers, home to nilgai, porcupine, mongoose, wolf and the occasional leopard. This is also one of the best places in Saurashtra to see the chinkara, the small Indian gazelle.

It is a nature education camp at heart. We walk the forest, learn to tell birds, animals and plants apart, visit the palace museum and the old village, and spend the night around a campfire.

faqs.question: Will we see wild animals?

faqs.question: When is Hingolgadh at its best?
faqs.answer: July to September, when the rains turn the hills green and the streams run. Winter mornings are good for birds.

faqs.question: Is it a good camp for younger students?

kutch.summary: Bhuj, the western coast, the White Rann and Mandvi: four days across India's largest district.
kutch.overview:
An old saying is printed on top of CNA's Kutch brochure: Sorath is best in winter, Gujarat in summer, the clouds in the monsoon, but Kutch is good all twelve months.

Kutch is India's largest district, and it does not look like the rest of Gujarat. Desert, salt flats, grassland, a long coast, palaces and craft villages all fit inside it. In four days we cover the heart of it: Bhuj and its palaces, the temples and wildlife sanctuary of the far west, the White Rann at Dhordo and the sea at Mandvi.

Our brochure says that on a full-moon night the White Rann feels as if the moon has come down to earth. Pick a batch near the full moon if you can.

itinerary.body: The Swaminarayan temple, the royal cenotaphs (Chhatardi) and Sharad Baug palace in Bhuj. Then west to the Koteshwar temple by the sea and the Narayan Sarovar wildlife sanctuary.

itinerary.body: Morning drive to Kalo Dungar, the highest point in Kutch, for a view over the Rann. Afternoon on to Dhordo for sunset and moonrise on the white salt desert.

itinerary.title: Mandvi and home
itinerary.body: Pingleshwar beach, Madreshwar and the Vijay Vilas palace at Mandvi, then the bus home in the evening.

saputara.summary: Five monsoon days in the Dang forest: waterfalls, caves, Vansda National Park and Gujarat's only hill station.
saputara.overview:
Have you ever stood at a Gujarat waterfall in full flow? Not a trickle over rocks, but a wall of brown water so loud you have to shout. In the Dang forest in August, that is a normal Tuesday.

Saputara sits at about 873 m in the Sahyadri hills of Dang district, ringed by forest, streams and small tribal villages. In the rainy season the whole area turns a deep green, mist rolls over the hills, and the waterfalls at Gira and around Saputara come alive.

We base ourselves in Saputara and go out every day: viewpoints and the museum, a forest walk in Vansda National Park, the Pandava caves and the waterfalls. Easy days, wet shoes, lots of green.

itinerary.body: Sunrise Point before breakfast. Then Gira waterfall, the botanical garden and a forest walk in Vansda National Park, with packed lunch. Back to the hotel by evening.

diu.summary: Three days of beach walks, caves and a Portuguese sea fort on the island the old texts called Dev Patan.
diu.overview:
Diu's old name was Dev Patan. The story goes that the gods themselves chose this little island to wander around. After a day on its beaches, you start to see their point.

Diu sits off the south coast of Saurashtra, joined to Gujarat by a bridge. The Portuguese held it for more than four centuries, until 1961, and left behind a huge fort on the sea, white churches and a town plan that still feels different from the mainland.

We keep it simple and on foot. A coastal walk to Nagoa beach, the caves near the fort, a sea-washed Shiva temple at Fudam and long evenings by the water. Easy, safe walking for groups of every age.

faqs.question: Is Diu a good trip for families?

faqs.question: What is special about Gangeshwar?
faqs.answer: It is a small Shiva temple in the rocks at Fudam. At high tide the sea washes over the five lingas, so time your visit with the tide.

gir-diu.summary: Girnar, the Gir forest, Diu's beaches and Somnath: four days across the south of Saurashtra.
gir-diu.overview:
Start the first morning in a cable car rising over Girnar. Spend the next day on forest trails in Gir. By day three your feet are in the Arabian Sea at Diu.

This trip strings together four very different places in the south of Saurashtra. Junagadh has Girnar and the Uparkot fort, which goes back more than 2,000 years and hides stepwells and Buddhist caves inside its walls. Sasan Gir is the last wild home of the Asiatic lion. Diu brings a Portuguese sea fort and long beaches, and Somnath closes the loop with its temple on the shore.

It is a lot of ground, but the pace stays easy. Two nights in tents near Sasan, one by the sea in Diu, and a campfire to end the forest day.

Jamjir and the Gayatri temple trail

itinerary.body: Morning forest walk in Gir. Lunch and a short rest. Afternoon around Talala and Devalia, with the Jamjir waterfall and the Gayatri temple. Campfire after dinner.

itinerary.body: Drive to Diu after breakfast. Diu Fort, St Paul's church, the caves and Jalandhar beach. After lunch, Nagoa and Gomti beaches till sunset. Night in Diu.

itinerary.title: Somnath and home

faqs.question: How long is the Girnar ropeway ride?
faqs.answer: A few minutes each way, and the view over the Girnar hills is one of the best in Gujarat. People who do not like heights can wait at the base with a leader.

faqs.question: Is this a good trip if I only have four days?
faqs.answer: Yes. You get a hill, a forest, a beach and a temple town in one trip, with easy walking and no long treks.

faqs.answer: Lions live all around Sasan, but they are wild. On a forest walk you are more likely to see deer, nilgai and birds. A jeep safari gives the best chance of a lion.

dwarka-somnath-diu.summary: Four days down the Saurashtra coast, with three sunsets over the Arabian Sea.
dwarka-somnath-diu.overview:
Count the sunsets. The first one goes down behind the Dwarka lighthouse. The second turns the sea gold beside Somnath. The third you watch with sand between your toes on Nagoa beach in Diu.

This trip follows the Saurashtra shore from its western tip to its southern edge. Dwarka sits where the Gomti meets the sea. Bet Dwarka is a short hop across the water. Somnath stands right on the shoreline, and Diu ends the trip with a Portuguese fort and quiet beaches.

The temples are part of the story, but the sea is the thread. We walk the beaches, stop at the Blue Flag beach at Shivrajpur, and keep the evenings for the water.

itinerary.body: Morning at the Somnath temple and the shore walk behind it. Short drive to Diu. Afternoon at Diu Fort, then sunset on Nagoa beach.

itinerary.title: Diu and home
itinerary.body: A morning walk through the caves and Gangeshwar Mahadev at Fudam, then the bus back to Rajkot.

dwarka-somnath.overview:
At Somnath there is an old pillar on the sea wall with an arrow pointing south. Its inscription says there is no land in a straight line from here to the South Pole. Look at a map later. It checks out.

This is the short version of the Saurashtra coast: three days, two famous temple towns and a lot of sea air. Dwarka sits where the Gomti river meets the Arabian Sea. Somnath faces open water. In between runs a coast road past fishing villages and long beaches.

We add Bet Dwarka island and Shivrajpur beach on the way, and keep the evenings for aarti, the shore and the sunset.

rann-of-kutch-dholavira.summary: A 4,500-year-old Harappan city, a park of tree fossils and sunset on the white salt desert.
rann-of-kutch-dholavira.overview:
How do you build a city in a desert? The people of Dholavira answered that 4,500 years ago. They cut huge stone reservoirs into the rock and caught every drop of rain that fell.

Dholavira sits on Khadir Bet, an island of land in the Great Rann of Kutch. It was one of the largest cities of the Harappan civilisation, and in 2021 it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site. You can still walk its streets, see the water tanks and stand where its gate once stood.

Close by is a fossil park with tree trunks turned to stone millions of years ago. Then we cross Kutch to Dhordo for the other wonder of this land: the white salt desert at sunset.

white-rann-of-kutch.summary: Sunset and moonrise on white salt, the view from Kalo Dungar and the craft villages of Banni.
white-rann-of-kutch.overview:
Plan this one by the calendar, not the clock. On a full-moon night the salt glows so bright that you can read your own shadow. Our old brochure put it best: it feels as if the moon has come down to earth.

For half the year the Great Rann of Kutch is a shallow sheet of water. When it dries, from about November, it leaves behind a flat crust of white salt that runs to the horizon. Dhordo, at its edge, is where we walk out onto it.

We give the Rann two evenings, climb Kalo Dungar for the view across it, and spend time in the villages of Banni, where embroidery, mud-and-mirror work and round bhunga homes are still part of daily life.

manali-snow-camp.summary: Learn to ski and snowboard on the winter slopes near Manali, with our own campus as your warm base.
manali-snow-camp.overview:
In 1996 our founder, Dr. Ketankumar Trivedi, finished a basic snow skiing course run by the Himachal government. He came back to Gujarat convinced that young people from the plains should feel real snow under their feet, not just see it in films. This camp is that idea, still running.

From January to the middle of March, the slopes around Solang near Manali stay under snow. Trained instructors start with the basics: how to stand on skis, how to stop and how to fall without getting hurt. By the last day most first-timers are sliding down a gentle slope on their own. Some switch to a snowboard and never switch back.

Evenings are slow and warm. You come back to our own campus at Vashisht, eat a hot meal and sit together while the cold settles on the valley.

astro-adventure-manali.summary: Trek, climb and raft in Manali by day. Read the night sky by night. The Adventure Olympiad scholarship camp.
astro-adventure-manali.overview:
When did you last see the Milky Way? For most people who grew up in a city, the honest answer is never.

This camp fixes that. Our base is our own campus at Vashisht, above Manali. By day you trek to Jogini waterfall, climb and rappel on real rock, cross a mountain river on a rope and raft the Beas. The big day is the trek up towards Bhrigu lake, with a night at a high camp near 4,000 m. By night, when the sky is clear, we set up telescopes and learn to find planets, stars and constellations.

It is also a digital detox. Phones stay away for most of the day, and you notice how much more you see without one. Our instructors have 20+ years of trekking experience and every camper goes home with a certificate.

This is the camp the Adventure Olympiad scholarships are for. Top scorers can win up to a 100% scholarship on the camp fee.

ladakh-trek.summary: A high-desert trek through river valleys and over a pass, with Leh as your base.
ladakh-trek.overview:
The first rule of Ladakh is simple: on day one, you do nothing.

Leh sits at about 3,500 m. You land there from the plains in an hour, but your body needs two full days to catch up. So we rest, walk slowly to a stupa, drink lots of water and only then head for the trail.

The trek itself is a different world from the green Himalaya. Bare brown mountains, a cold river beside you, villages with barley fields and white-washed houses, and nights so clear the stars look close. The big day takes you over a high pass with wide views of the Ladakh ranges. It is hard work. That is why it feels so good.

faqs.question: What is altitude sickness and how do you handle it?
faqs.answer: Headache, tiredness and poor sleep can come when you go high too fast. We prevent it with two rest days in Leh, a slow pace and lots of water. If someone feels unwell, our leaders take them down. Going down is the cure.

faqs.question: How do I train for this trek?
faqs.answer: Start 6 to 8 weeks before. Brisk walks or jogging most days, stairs with a loaded backpack and some leg strength work. If you can walk 5 km in 40 minutes, you are on track.

faqs.question: How cold is Ladakh in summer?
faqs.answer: Days can be warm and sunny. Nights at camp can drop close to freezing. Layers matter more than one heavy jacket.

faqs.question: Is there mobile network on the trail?
faqs.answer: Mostly no. In Leh, postpaid connections usually work but prepaid SIMs from other states often do not, so check before you fly. Our leaders carry a plan for emergencies.

leh-ladakh-circuit.summary: Over Khardung La to the Nubra dunes, then a night by the blue water of Pangong lake.
leh-ladakh-circuit.overview:
Sit by Pangong lake for an hour and watch the water change colour: deep blue, then green, then grey when a cloud passes, then blue again.

Ladakh lies between the Great Himalaya and the Karakoram. Summers are short and bright; in winter even Leh drops to minus 20 °C. This circuit is built for that short summer. We cross Khardung La, one of the highest roads in the world, drop into the Nubra valley with its sand dunes and two-humped camels, then follow the Shyok river to Pangong.

You walk less here than on a trek, but the altitude is just as real. That is why we start with full rest days in Leh and keep the pace slow. On the way you will see monasteries, river confluences and some of the darkest night skies in India.

grand-uttaranchal-trek.summary: Raft 12 km of the Ganga, walk up to Neelkanth, see Mussoorie and look for elephants in Rajaji.
grand-uttaranchal-trek.overview:
Twelve kilometres. About three hours. That is the stretch of the Ganga we raft, from Shivpuri down to Rishikesh, and nobody stays dry.

Uttarakhand is called Dev Bhumi, the land of the gods, and this trip shows you why in a week. After the river, we trek up through forest to the Neelkanth temple and carry our lunch with us. Next comes Mussoorie, the hill town above Dehradun, with long walks and views towards the high peaks.

The last morning starts before sunrise, in an open jeep inside Rajaji National Park. Elephants, deer, peacocks and, if you are very lucky, a leopard. It is an easy trip with a lot packed in, and a good first Himalayan trip for groups.

nainital-almora-binsar.summary: Three nights at a forest camp near Binsar, then Nainital lake and a jungle safari in Corbett.
nainital-almora-binsar.overview:
The Chand kings of Kumaon once ruled from Binsar in summer. Today the forest has gone back to the birds.

Binsar stands at about 2,100 m, in thick oak and rhododendron forest. On a clear morning the whole line of the Himalaya shows up across the horizon, peak after peak. Our camp here is a base for three days of real outdoor life: a day trek to Binsar, rock climbing and rappelling with our instructors, bird walks and campfires at night.

Then we come down to Nainital, a town built around a lake, and finish in Corbett National Park, India's oldest national park, with a jungle safari. It is a long trip, but an easy one, and it gives you time to slow down.

faqs.answer: The Kumaon forests are home to many Himalayan birds: woodpeckers, laughingthrushes, barbets and, with luck, the koklass or kalij pheasant. Our leaders help you spot them.

faqs.question: Is a tiger sighting guaranteed in Corbett?

nainital-mussoorie-corbett.summary: Two hill towns and India's oldest national park, at an easy, walking pace.
nainital-mussoorie-corbett.overview:
India's first national park opened in 1936, in the forests along the Ramganga river. Today it carries the name of Jim Corbett, a hunter from Nainital who put down his gun and spent the rest of his life asking people to save the tiger.

This trip follows his country. We start in Mussoorie, with walks along Camel's Back Road and down to the waterfalls. Then we drop to the Corbett forest for a morning safari and a quiet walk by the Kosi river. The last stop is Nainital, the lake town where Corbett grew up, with a boat on the lake and a walk up to a Himalayan viewpoint.

It is an easy trip with no hard climbs. You will walk every day, though, and spend more time under trees than in shops.

shimla-manali-amritsar.overview:
Snow peaks at breakfast. A langar meal with thousands of strangers at dinner. Few trips change scene as fast as this one.

We start in Shimla, the summer capital of British India, walking the Ridge and the pine forest trails around it. Then the road climbs into the Kullu valley to Manali, where we spend our days by the Beas, in the deodar forest around Hadimba and in the meadows of Solang.

The last stop is Amritsar. The Golden Temple's community kitchen feeds tens of thousands of people every day, free, with volunteers rolling rotis side by side. You eat sitting on the floor with everyone else. In the evening, we watch the flag ceremony at the Attari border. It is a good trip for groups who want the mountains and a slice of history in one week.

kullu-shimla-manali.overview:
Why do people call Kullu the Valley of the Gods? Almost every village here has its own deity. During the Kullu Dussehra in October, hundreds of them are carried down to the town on palanquins, with drums and horns.

This is a short, classic Himachal loop. We start with walks on the ridges of Shimla, then follow the road up the Kullu valley, past apple orchards and pine forest. In Kullu we spend a day on the Beas in a raft. Near Manali, the Solang meadows give you big mountain views and, in spring, patches of snow.

Nights are at our own campus in Vashisht, so the food, the stay and the safety stay in our hands even on a short trip.

kullu-manali-dalhousie.summary: Up the Kullu valley to Manali, then west to the old hill town of Dalhousie and the meadow of Khajjiar.
kullu-manali-dalhousie.overview:
Dalhousie was built in the 1850s across five small hills and named after Lord Dalhousie, then Governor-General of India. The old churches and quiet roads are still there. So are the deodar trees, some of them taller than the churches.

This trip links two very different corners of Himachal. First the Kullu valley and Manali, with the Beas below you and snow peaks above. Then a long drive west to Dalhousie and, a short way beyond it, Khajjiar: an open green meadow ringed by deodar forest, often called the mini Switzerland of India.

Nights in Manali are at our own campus in Vashisht. Days are spent outdoors, walking meadows and forest paths rather than queuing at viewpoints.

sikkim-trek.summary: Gangtok on foot, the glacial Tsomgo lake at 3,750 m and a short raft on the Teesta.
sikkim-trek.overview:
In 2016 Sikkim became India's first fully organic state. No chemical fertilisers, no chemical pesticides, across the whole state. You can taste it in the food.

It is a small mountain state with a huge range: from about 300 m in the river valleys to 8,586 m at Kanchenjunga, India's highest peak. The Lepcha, Bhutia and Nepali communities live here side by side, and their monasteries, prayer flags and food are part of every day.

Our base is Gangtok. We walk the town and its monastery, spend a morning on the forest trails of the Himalayan Zoological Park, where red pandas and Himalayan black bears live in big open enclosures, and drive up to Tsomgo lake at 3,750 m. On the way back down to the plains we raft a short stretch of the Teesta.

everest-base-camp.summary: Walk the Khumbu valley of Nepal to the foot of Everest (5,364 m) and watch sunrise from Kala Patthar (5,644 m).
everest-base-camp.overview:
The trek starts with a 35-minute flight into Lukla (2,860 m), onto a short runway cut into the side of a mountain. Everybody goes quiet on the landing. Then they start talking about it for the next two weeks.

From Lukla you walk up the Khumbu valley, crossing the Dudh Koshi river on long suspension bridges and climbing through Sherpa villages to Namche Bazaar (3,440 m). Prayer flags, yak trains, stone walls and, on a clear morning, your first look at Everest. Higher up come the Tengboche monastery (3,867 m), the open valley of Dingboche (4,410 m) and the moraine camps of Lobuche (4,940 m) and Gorak Shep (5,164 m).

Base Camp sits on the Khumbu glacier at 5,364 m. The best view of Everest, though, comes the next morning: a slow climb in the dark to Kala Patthar (5,644 m), with Everest, Nuptse, Lhotse and Pumori lighting up one by one.

We go slowly on purpose. Two full rest days help your body adjust to the thin air, and our leaders watch every member of the group for signs of altitude sickness.

faqs.question: What about altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: It can affect anyone, fit or not. We climb slowly, take two rest days and keep checking on you. If someone feels unwell, they go down with a leader. Going down is the cure.

faqs.question: Do I need a passport for Nepal?
faqs.answer: Indian citizens can enter Nepal with a valid passport or voter ID card. Carry the original. An Aadhaar card alone is not enough.

faqs.question: Will my phone work up there?
faqs.answer: Mobile signal comes and goes, and most lodges sell Wi-Fi and charging by the hour. Carry a power bank and tell your family you may go quiet for a day or two.

faqs.question: What if the Lukla flight is delayed?
faqs.answer: It happens. Mountain flights only fly in clear weather. Our leaders reshuffle the plan, and any extra cost from delays is shared as per our terms.

mount-abu.summary: Climb and rappel at Toad Rock, then watch the sun drop behind the Aravallis from Rajasthan's only hill station.
mount-abu.overview:
Want to try rock climbing but only have a long weekend? This is the trip.

Mount Abu sits at about 1,220 m in the Aravalli hills, a cool green island in dry Rajasthan. Guru Shikhar, the highest point of the Aravallis at about 1,722 m, is a short drive away. The marble Dilwara Jain temples are here, and so is Nakki lake, ringed by hills and old rocks.

One of those rocks is shaped like a frog about to jump into the lake. That is Toad Rock, and it is our climbing wall. Our instructors fix the ropes, show you the holds and stay with you on every move up and every step down.

Evenings are slow: a walk by the lake, Sunset Point and a campfire with the group.

rajasthan-heritage.summary: Udaipur's lakes, Jaipur's forts, the blue lanes of Jodhpur and a golden fort on the edge of the Thar.
rajasthan-heritage.overview:
A few kilometres outside Jaisalmer, in the middle of the desert, lie trunks of trees that turned to stone millions of years ago. This dry land was once forest. Standing at the Akal Wood Fossil Park, it is hard to believe, and that is exactly why we take you there.

The trail crosses the state. It starts in Udaipur, the lake city founded by Maharana Udai Singh II in 1559. Then Jaipur, the Pink City laid out in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II, with Amber fort on the hill and Jal Mahal floating in its lake. Then Jodhpur, and finally Jaisalmer, a living fort of yellow sandstone on Trikut hill, founded by Rawal Jaisal around 1156.

Between the forts and havelis we spend time in the Desert National Park, where the Thar shows its quieter side: dunes, scrub and desert birds. The last night ends with a Rajasthani folk evening.

lonavala.summary: Fort treks, dam walks and green Sahyadri hills around the hill town of Lonavala.
lonavala.overview:
Come in August and the Sahyadri hills look as if someone opened a hundred taps at once. Every slope runs with white water, every hollow becomes a pond, and the clouds sit low enough to walk through.

Lonavala sits at about 625 m in the Western Ghats, between Mumbai and Pune. The monsoon from June to September makes it green; the cool, clear winters make it good for treks. Either way, there is a fort or a hill every day.

We climb Tiger Hill for the valley view, walk up to Korigad fort and around its old walls, and spend a day by Pawna lake with a nature session on the Western Ghats: rain, rocks, frogs, birds and why these hills matter to half of India's rivers.

panchgani-mahabaleshwar.summary: Five hills, a flat-topped plateau and the valley where the Krishna river begins.
panchgani-mahabaleshwar.overview:
The Krishna river runs about 1,300 km across India to the Bay of Bengal. It starts as a small spring at a temple in Old Mahabaleshwar, a few minutes' walk from where we stand on Day 4.

Panchgani, at about 1,334 m, is named after the five hills around it. The road up winds past viewpoints over the Krishna valley on one side and the plains on the other. Old British bungalows, Parsi homes and boarding schools give the town a quiet, slow feel.

We walk the forest trails here, cross Table Land (one of the largest volcanic plateaus in Asia, flat as a cricket ground) and go down to Dhom dam on the Krishna. Mahabaleshwar, a little higher, gives us the big viewpoints and the old temple where the river begins.

pachmarhi.overview:
Pachmarhi has no lazy days.

The town sits in a bowl of the Satpura hills, about 1,000 m up, surrounded by thick sal and teak forest, sandstone cliffs and deep ravines. Leopards, wild boar, langurs and peacocks live in these forests, and rare orchids grow on the wet rocks. Locals call it Satpura ki Rani, the queen of the Satpuras.

Every day we walk to something: a waterfall, a pool you can sit in, a cave temple or a hilltop. Apsara Vihar, Rajat Prapat, Jata Shankar, Handi Khoh. On the last full day we climb to Dhoopgarh, the highest point in Madhya Pradesh, for the sunset.

Expect steps, rocky paths and wet feet. Expect to sleep very well.

jabalpur-kanha.summary: Safari in the sal forests of Kanha, then a boat through the white marble gorge of the Narmada.
jabalpur-kanha.overview:
Mowgli's forest is real. You can drive into it.

Rudyard Kipling set The Jungle Book in the central Indian forests, and Kanha is the one most people picture: tall sal trees, open grassy meadows and herds of deer moving through the morning mist. It is one of India's best-known tiger reserves.

Kanha also saved a species. The hard-ground barasingha, a swamp deer with up to twelve tines on its antlers, was down to a few dozen animals here. Today it lives in Kanha in the hundreds, and you will likely see it on the meadows. Keep your binoculars ready too: the park has around 175 kinds of birds.

On the way home we stop at Bhedaghat near Jabalpur, where the Narmada cuts through cliffs of white marble. A boat takes you through the gorge, and a short walk leads to the roar of Dhuandhar falls.

goa.summary: Long beaches, sea forts and old churches, plus a jungle trek to the white curtain of Dudhsagar falls.
goa.overview:
Most people go to Goa for the sea. We keep one whole day for the jungle.

Inland, where the Western Ghats rise near the Karnataka border, the Mandovi river drops off a cliff in four tiers. The water is so white it got the name Dudhsagar, the sea of milk. We trek through the forest to reach it, and it is the day most campers talk about on the train home.

The coast gets its share too. North Goa's long beaches from Arambol to Candolim, Aguada fort above the sea, the quieter sands of South Goa, and Old Goa, where churches from the 1500s stand next to temples. East and west have lived side by side here for a long time, and you see it in the buildings, the food and the festivals.

Evenings are easy: Dona Paula and Miramar at sunset, and a slow walk through Panaji.

kerala.summary: Fort Kochi, the tea hills of Munnar, Thekkady's spice forest and the backwaters of Alleppey.
kerala.overview:
Why did Roman ships sail all the way to a small coast in south India? Pepper. Kerala's spices were worth so much that Greeks, Romans, Arabs, Chinese and later the Portuguese, Dutch and British all came here to trade, and every one of them left something behind.

You see it on Day 3 in Fort Kochi: Chinese fishing nets on the shore, a 16th-century synagogue in Mattancherry, and St. Francis Church, among the oldest European churches in India.

Then the land rises. Kerala is a narrow strip between the Arabian Sea and the Western Ghats, with 44 rivers running down. We drive up past waterfalls into the tea hills of Munnar, walk in Eravikulam National Park (home of the rare Nilgiri tahr, a mountain goat), take a boat on the lake at Thekkady and visit a spice garden. The trip ends on flat water: the backwaters and beach of Alleppey, and Kovalam on the way out.

karnataka.summary: A rock day and a tent night at Ramanagara, Mysore palace, and three days in the coffee hills of Coorg.
karnataka.overview:
If the granite hills on Day 4 look familiar, that is because you have seen them in Sholay. Ramanagara's giant boulders were Gabbar Singh's hideout. Today they are one of South India's favourite places to learn rock climbing.

That is where our trip really starts. After a day in Bengaluru, we spend a full day on the rocks: rappelling, chimney climbing, bouldering, face climbing and a zip line, with our instructors. Then a campfire and a night in tents under the boulders.

From there the trail turns green. Mysore for the palace, Chamundi hill and KRS dam. Then three days in Coorg, India's coffee country: Iruppu falls, the Tibetan settlement and Golden Temple at Bylakuppe, Nagarhole's forests, and Talakaveri, the hill where the Kaveri river begins. The last climb is a forest trek to Nishani Motte.

odisha.summary: Crocodile creeks in Bhitarkanika, dolphins on Chilika lake and the Sun Temple at Konark.
odisha.overview:
The boat slows down in a narrow creek. On the mud bank there are three grey logs. Then one of them opens its eyes.

Bhitarkanika, on the Odisha coast, is one of India's largest mangrove forests and home to the country's biggest population of saltwater crocodiles. We go into its creeks by boat on Day 3 to look for them, along with monitor lizards, spotted deer and kingfishers.

Further south, Chilika lake meets the sea. It is Asia's largest brackish-water lagoon, and at Satapada, where the water opens to the Bay of Bengal, rare Irrawaddy dolphins come up to breathe. Early the next morning we take a boat out to the birds and Kalijai island.

Between the wild places, Odisha's temple country: the old shrines of Bhubaneswar, Jagannath at Puri, the stone chariot of the Sun Temple at Konark, and the Jain caves of Udayagiri. Then the hot springs of Taptapani in the hills and the quiet beach at Gopalpur.

faqs.question: Is the Bhitarkanika boat ride safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. You stay in a covered boat with a local boatman and forest rules: hands inside, no feeding, no getting off on the banks. The crocodiles keep to the mud.

faqs.question: Are the Chilika dolphins always there?
faqs.answer: Usually, around Satapada, but they surface for a moment and dive again. Patience helps. Early mornings and calm water are best.

faqs.question: Can everyone enter the Jagannath temple?
faqs.answer: Only Hindus are allowed inside the Puri temple. Others can see it from outside, and our leaders will plan time for everyone.

faqs.question: Is Odisha hot?
faqs.answer: From October to February it is pleasant. Summers are hot and humid, which is why we suggest winter batches.
